name: 555 Edgecombe Avenue
short_description: A 1916 beaux-arts apartment building in Washington Heights that became a hub of African American cultural life by the 1940s, home to Joe Louis, Lena Horne, Count Basie, Duke Ellington, and Billy Strayhorn.

discovery_sources: Lonely Planet New York City (12th ed, 2022)
_pipeline.discovery_notes: Extracted from LP chunks: chunk-09. gravity: Historically significant African American cultural landmark; residents included boxing champion Joe Louis and major jazz figures; site of legendary ongoing Sunday jazz jams by Marjorie Eliot.

gravity_audit.reasoning: LP new POI. Notability composite 52 from agent-extraction prominence, guidebook (Lonely Planet) presence. Ranked relative to all 286 NYC POIs; assigned gravity 2.

beats.script_body: When completed in 1916, this brick beaux-arts giant at 555 Edgecombe Avenue was Washington Heights' first luxury apartment complex, with a concierge, a separate workers' entrance, and no fewer than three elevators. It was initially available only to whites, but the neighborhood's transformation from predominantly Irish and Jewish to African American saw the building's residents become mostly Black by the 1940s. Its tenants would include some of New York's most prominent African Americans, among them boxer Joe Louis and music heavyweights Lena Horne, Count Basie, Duke Ellington, and Billy Strayhorn.

name: Abyssinian Baptist Church
short_description: Harlem's most famous gospel church, known for its celebrated Sunday tourist gospel services running from mid-September through July with strict visitor dress codes.

discovery_sources: Lonely Planet New York City (12th ed, 2022)
_pipeline.discovery_notes: Extracted from LP chunks: chunk-09. gravity: Most famous gospel church in Harlem; dedicated tourist gospel services; culturally significant African American religious institution; major visitor attraction.

beats.script_body: What started as an occasional pilgrimage has turned into a tourist-industry spectacle: entire busloads of travelers now make their way to Harlem every Sunday to attend a gospel service. The volume of visitors is so high that some churches turn away people due to space constraints. In some cases, tourists have been known to outnumber congregants. Naturally, this has led to friction — many locals are upset by visitors who chat during sermons, leave in the middle of services, or show up in skimpy attire. If you do attend, be respectful: dress modestly, don't take pictures, and remain for the duration. The most famous services are the soulful Sunday gospel services at Abyssinian Baptist Church, running mid-September through July. Arrive at least an hour before the 11:30am tourist service to queue up.

beats.poi_name: Cathedral of St. John the Divine
beats.script_body: The largest place of worship in America has yet to be completed — and probably won't be anytime soon. But this glorious Episcopal cathedral commands attention with its ornate Gothic-style facade, booming vintage organ, and extravagantly scaled nave — twice as wide as London's Westminster Abbey. The first cornerstone was laid on St John's Day in 1892, but construction was hardly smooth. Engineers had to dig 70 feet in order to find bedrock to anchor the building. Architects died or were fired, and in 1911, the initial Romanesque design was exchanged for a bigger, Gothic-inspired plan. Depleted funds have seen construction regularly halted. The north tower remains unbuilt, and a 'temporary' domed roof constructed out of terracotta tile in 1909 still rises above the epicenter of the church. If it is ever completed, the 601-foot-long cathedral will rank as the world's third-largest church, behind Rome's St Peter's Basilica and Côte d'Ivoire's Basilica of Our Lady of Peace at Yamoussoukro.

The first cornerstone for the cathedral was laid on St John's Day in 1892, but construction was hardly smooth. Engineers had to dig 70ft in order to find bedrock to which they could anchor the building. If it is ever completed, the 601ft-long cathedral will rank as the world's third-largest church, behind Rome's St Peter's Basilica and Côte d'Ivoire's Basilica of Our Lady of Peace at Yamoussoukro.

beats.script_body: Behind the choir is the white-gold and bronze triptych Life of Christ, carved by '80s pop artist Keith Haring, who lived from 1958 to 1990. beats.script_body: Founded in Lower Manhattan in 1754 as King's College, the oldest university in New York is now one of the world's premier research institutions. name: Studio Museum in Harlem
short_description: A treasured Harlem museum showcasing influential African American artists, serving as a cultural hub for rotating exhibitions, film screenings, and gallery talks.

discovery_sources: Lonely Planet New York City (12th ed, 2022)

beats.script_body: For more than 40 years, this treasured museum has showcased influential African American artists. The permanent collection is small — just under 2000 objects — but rich. The Studio Museum has been an important patron to African American artists, and the collection features work by more than 400 of them. This includes important pieces by painter Jacob Lawrence, photographer Gordon Parks, and collagist Romare Bearden — all represented in major museum collections in the US. Additional works include those by a new generation of artists, such as Nigeria-born Njideka Akunyili Crosby, who was awarded a MacArthur Genius Award in 2017 for her large-scale collage and photo transfer-based paintings.

beats.source_passage: For more than 40 years, this treasured museum has showcased influential African American artists. Yet it's not just another art display center – it is a significant point of connection for a breadth of Harlem cultural figures, who enjoy a rotating selection of exhibitions, film screenings, gallery talks and more. The permanent collection is small (just under 2000 objects), but it is rich. The Studio Museum has been an important patron to African American artists, and the collection features work by more than 400 of them. This includes important pieces by painter Jacob Lawrence, photographer Gordon Parks and collagist Romare Bearden – all of whom are represented in major museum collections in the US. Additional works include those by a new generation of artists, such as Nigeria-born Njideka Akunyili Crosby, who was awarded a MacArthur Genius Award in 2017 for her large-scale collage and photo transfer-based paintings that navigate the cultural complexities of the transnational experience.

beats.script_body: Among the Cloisters' many rare treasures is the beguiling tapestry series The Hunt of the Unicorn, dating from 1495 to 1505. Also worth seeking out is the remarkably well-preserved 15th-century Annunciation Triptych, also called the Merode Altarpiece.
